tools.name: open_panel
tools.description:
Show the user a side panel in MindRoom Chat: 'computer' or 'members'.
panel='computer' opens the Computer panel: a live view of your own worker
browser, the one browser_control drives with target='host'. The user starts
out watching. They can take control, for example to log in; while they have
it your browser calls are blocked, and when they hand it back you get a
message. Opening the panel does not navigate to a URL, send a prompt to
ChatGPT, or take control, and it never opens or controls the user's own
browser. Your first worker browser call in a conversation (browser_control
with target='host', or any browser_mcp function) already shows the user this
panel; call open_panel(panel='computer') only to show it again in a later
reply, for example when the user should log in or after they closed it. One
reply shows the panel once.

panel='members' opens the Members panel, listing the people and agents in
this room.

Success means the UI request was sent, not that the client opened a panel.

panel.description: 'computer' for your worker browser, or 'members' (the default) for this room's members.

mindroom_output_path.description: Optional workspace-relative path: save the full supported output there and return a short receipt.

This works on the Chat app's own settings screen. It changes no setting; the
user decides what to do there. Success means the UI request was sent, not that
the client opened Settings.

tools.description:
Run the call a scheduled task stored, once, with the requester's approval.
Call this when a scheduled task asks you to. It runs the stored call without
another approval card and returns the tool's result. If the requester approved
any arguments, you may pass arguments_json to replace the stored arguments for
the same tool; otherwise omit it.

task_id.description: The scheduled task's ID from its message.

arguments_json.description:
Optional replacement arguments as a JSON object string,
only when the requester approved any arguments.

mindroom_output_path.description: Optional workspace-relative path: save the full supported output there and return a short receipt.

tools.name: run_subagent
tools.description:
Run one allowed configured agent as a fresh subagent and wait for its result.
Allowed subagents for this caller: researcher.
Use only these agent names. Include all relevant context, constraints, and expected output in task; the child does not inherit this conversation. It keeps its configured tools, workspace, and memory.
Selecting your own name starts a fresh copy of yourself, if listed. Omit agent_name or pass null to select yourself; the same allowlist applies. Set model to a configured model name to override the child's model for this session. Available models: default. Omit model or pass null to use the child's normal thread, room, or configured model. The caller waits; this does not create a Matrix thread. Use continue_subagent with the returned subagent_id for follow-ups in the same child session; follow-ups keep the child's model and mode.
In Matrix, approval-required child tools pause for the user's approval before continuing. Returns the child's answer, stable subagent ID, and an audit reference scoped to the child agent.

task.description: Self-contained task with relevant context, constraints, and expected output.

agent_name.description: Allowed subagent name; omitted or null selects yourself, if allowed.

model.description: Configured model name from models; omitted or null uses normal model selection.

title.description: Short title of 3-6 words naming the task, shown to people watching the run.

mindroom_output_path.description: Optional workspace-relative path: save the full supported output there and return a short receipt.

tools.name: schedule
tools.description:
Schedule a one-time or recurring task with structured timing parameters.
Provide exactly one of `execute_at`, `delay_seconds`, or `cron`.

message.description:
Exact trigger message posted when the schedule fires (non-empty).
Include `@agent_name` or `@team_name` if targeting specific responders.

new_thread.description:
Required delivery choice. Use `False` to post in the current
room/thread scope. Use `True` to start a fresh thread per fire: each
fire posts a room-level root and the responding agent answers in a
new thread under it with a fresh session. When `silent=True`, the
trigger stays hidden instead, and any finding or failure is posted
as a room-level root rather than beneath the hidden trigger.

execute_at.description:
One-time run timestamp as an ISO 8601 datetime with a time
component (e.g. "2026-11-25T09:00:00-08:00", "...Z", or naive
"2026-11-25T09:00:00" interpreted in `timezone`). Must be in the
future; include an explicit UTC offset during DST transitions.

delay_seconds.description:
One-time relative delay in positive seconds (>= 1),
e.g. 900 for 15 minutes, 3600 for 1 hour.

cron.description:
Recurring 5-field cron expression (`minute hour day month weekday`,
e.g. "0 9 * * 1-5"), evaluated in `timezone` (DST-safe).

description.description:
Optional short human-readable label for schedule listings;
defaults to trimmed `message`.

timezone.description:
Optional IANA timezone name (e.g. "America/Los_Angeles");
defaults to this agent's configured timezone.

history_limit.description:
Max recent thread messages included as context each time
the task fires. Use 0 for no history (recommended for recurring
polling tasks), or leave unset for unlimited history.

silent.description:
Keep the trigger hidden and omit a final response when it is empty,
whitespace-only, or ends with `NO_REPLY`. Findings, failures, and
independently sent tool messages remain visible. Defaults to `False`.

model.description:
Configured model alias for each scheduled run (including team
members), e.g. "cheap", or `name@level` for one of its reasoning
levels, e.g. "sol@high". Leave unset to use normal agent, room, and
thread model selection. This does not change the conversation model.

mindroom_output_path.description: Optional workspace-relative path: save the full supported output there and return a short receipt.

tools.name: schedule_tool_call
tools.description:
Schedule one of your approval-gated tool calls that the requester approves now.
Use this when a gated action, such as sending an external message, must run at
a set time while the requester may be away. MindRoom stores the call and posts an
approval card in this thread showing it and the send time. When the task fires,
you are asked to call `run_scheduled_call` with its task ID, which runs the stored
call once without another approval. Tell the requester to approve the card; do
not claim the call ran until `run_scheduled_call` reports its result.

tool_name.description: One of your tool functions, e.g. "post_slack_message".

arguments_json.description: The call's arguments as a JSON object string.

execute_at.description:
When to run, as ISO 8601 with a UTC offset,
e.g. "2026-10-04T09:00:00-04:00".

description.description:
Short description of the scheduled action; if the requester
approves any arguments, it tells you what the call should do when it runs.

mindroom_output_path.description: Optional workspace-relative path: save the full supported output there and return a short receipt.

reply, for example when the user should log in or after they closed it. One
reply shows the panel once.

panel='members' opens the Members panel, listing the people and agents in
this room.

Success means the UI request was sent, not that the client opened a panel.

panel.description: 'computer' for your worker browser, or 'members' (the default) for this room's members.

tools.name: run_scheduled_call
tools.description:
Run the call a scheduled task stored, once, with the requester's approval.
Call this when a scheduled task asks you to. It runs the stored call without
another approval card and returns the tool's result. If the requester approved
any arguments, you may pass arguments_json to replace the stored arguments for
the same tool; otherwise omit it.

task_id.description: The scheduled task's ID from its message.

arguments_json.description:
Optional replacement arguments as a JSON object string,
only when the requester approved any arguments.

mindroom_output_path.description: Optional workspace-relative path: save the full supported output there and return a short receipt.

tools.name: run_subagent
tools.description:
Run one allowed configured agent as a fresh subagent and wait for its result.
Allowed subagents for this caller: researcher.
Use only these agent names. Include all relevant context, constraints, and expected output in task; the child does not inherit this conversation. It keeps its configured tools, workspace, and memory.
Selecting your own name starts a fresh copy of yourself, if listed. Omit agent_name or pass null to select yourself; the same allowlist applies. Set model to a configured model name to override the child's model for this session. Available models: default. Omit model or pass null to use the child's normal thread, room, or configured model. The caller waits; this does not create a Matrix thread. Use continue_subagent with the returned subagent_id for follow-ups in the same child session; follow-ups keep the child's model and mode.
In Matrix, approval-required child tools pause for the user's approval before continuing. Returns the child's answer, stable subagent ID, and an audit reference scoped to the child agent.

task.description: Self-contained task with relevant context, constraints, and expected output.

agent_name.description: Allowed subagent name; omitted or null selects yourself, if allowed.

model.description: Configured model name from models; omitted or null uses normal model selection.

title.description: Short title of 3-6 words naming the task, shown to people watching the run.

mindroom_output_path.description: Optional workspace-relative path: save the full supported output there and return a short receipt.

tools.name: schedule
tools.description:
Schedule a one-time or recurring task with structured timing parameters.
Provide exactly one of `execute_at`, `delay_seconds`, or `cron`.

message.description:
Exact trigger message posted when the schedule fires (non-empty).
Include `@agent_name` or `@team_name` if targeting specific responders.

new_thread.description:
Required delivery choice. Use `False` to post in the current
room/thread scope. Use `True` to start a fresh thread per fire: each
fire posts a room-level root and the responding agent answers in a
new thread under it with a fresh session. When `silent=True`, the
trigger stays hidden instead, and any finding or failure is posted
as a room-level root rather than beneath the hidden trigger.

execute_at.description:
One-time run timestamp as an ISO 8601 datetime with a time
component (e.g. "2026-11-25T09:00:00-08:00", "...Z", or naive
"2026-11-25T09:00:00" interpreted in `timezone`). Must be in the
future; include an explicit UTC offset during DST transitions.

delay_seconds.description:
One-time relative delay in positive seconds (>= 1),
e.g. 900 for 15 minutes, 3600 for 1 hour.

cron.description:
Recurring 5-field cron expression (`minute hour day month weekday`,
e.g. "0 9 * * 1-5"), evaluated in `timezone` (DST-safe).

description.description:
Optional short human-readable label for schedule listings;
defaults to trimmed `message`.

timezone.description:
Optional IANA timezone name (e.g. "America/Los_Angeles");
defaults to this agent's configured timezone.

history_limit.description:
Max recent thread messages included as context each time
the task fires. Use 0 for no history (recommended for recurring
polling tasks), or leave unset for unlimited history.

silent.description:
Keep the trigger hidden and omit a final response when it is empty,
whitespace-only, or ends with `NO_REPLY`. Findings, failures, and
independently sent tool messages remain visible. Defaults to `False`.

model.description:
Configured model alias for each scheduled run (including team
members), e.g. "cheap", or `name@level` for one of its reasoning
levels, e.g. "sol@high". Leave unset to use normal agent, room, and
thread model selection. This does not change the conversation model.

mindroom_output_path.description: Optional workspace-relative path: save the full supported output there and return a short receipt.

tools.name: schedule_tool_call
tools.description:
Schedule one of your approval-gated tool calls that the requester approves now.
Use this when a gated action, such as sending an external message, must run at
a set time while the requester may be away. MindRoom stores the call and posts an
approval card in this thread showing it and the send time. When the task fires,
you are asked to call `run_scheduled_call` with its task ID, which runs the stored
call once without another approval. Tell the requester to approve the card; do
not claim the call ran until `run_scheduled_call` reports its result.

tool_name.description: One of your tool functions, e.g. "post_slack_message".

arguments_json.description: The call's arguments as a JSON object string.

execute_at.description:
When to run, as ISO 8601 with a UTC offset,
e.g. "2026-10-04T09:00:00-04:00".

description.description:
Short description of the scheduled action; if the requester
approves any arguments, it tells you what the call should do when it runs.

mindroom_output_path.description: Optional workspace-relative path: save the full supported output there and return a short receipt.
